d997ea98-f20a-4099-9ea6-49114a84cb7f.notes: Hi, I'm Viviana matsuda. Um, I do pottery for a living. My brand name is Mud Witch. Um, yeah. I'm a full time potter.

0b1cf930-3e62-4571-a8b0-34c78ce405d0.notes: Um, so my voice and style for mud, which it's kind of a funny thing where when I was learning to do ceramics, I was also learning about the body positivity movement.

4349ae73-65e4-48f6-8894-18746dab4c8c.notes: And I was like starting to make these like chubby shapes and they're literally called this is the Chubby Mug. This is the Venus mug

ba3e1a4b-861a-47e6-8fdb-cb1461f4de1a.notes: I think those two things kind of just mushed together the learning clay and the body positivity.

caee06c8-1059-4fd2-9d6b-752d4854719e.notes: they were originally supposed to be kind of like an abstract like vision of, of people, like different bodies sitting, dancing, whatever.

0080bb87-4fb7-4f7f-a373-553f282fa1b8.notes: so I used like 11 different types of clay, and they were all the range of skin tones. Um, so they were like naked.

2365676d-e85c-4f1a-bf13-22005ed12ac4.notes: and then I was like, well, let's slap some color on these, um, let's clothe these babes.

a57f372d-3d7e-4174-a29e-a6d1d989fac0.notes: I, It started off as one thing, and now it's just like, I just want to make something that, like, makes people smile.

84c9bbb6-1e6e-49ed-a477-f1b41dcf1286.notes: Like, there's something called the artist's hand where when you, um, hand-built something or we'll throw it, you can kind of feel where the artist's hands have been.

c1771688-d185-42ea-a640-0fe561fa5559.notes: and I think that that is very important because we, you know, in society, we're like, so becoming more and more disconnected to, like human interaction in especially, like, touch or anything along those lines.

b4f92bc2-f20b-4163-92ca-fe0f2e814dfc.notes: I think that it's so easy to desire so many things, um, that we actually don't need.

a5960a28-85e8-48a0-8562-172247ec8823.notes: Um, but also just the value of keeping something for a very long time.

5103dc13-e586-4808-821b-2726b83080bf.notes: with lockdown, people really sat in their houses and realized that the things that were surrounding them weren't bringing them joy. And I think that's why ceramics has had such a big surge.

8e3b8d4d-6e17-46be-88ea-07c38bad633b.notes: the pendulum is really swinging in both ways, where people are really like, I want a select few things that I know will bring me happiness in my house. And then the pendulum swings the other way with like extreme fast fashion, temu shi and nonsense, where you can get like 80 mugs for whatever, a doll or whatever.

4038e308-c469-47f3-8b7d-1c62b9650e98.notes: But not only that, but like, you don't need all of that stuff. Like, you could literally just get a couple things that make you happy.

9dc55ef6-bf4e-4601-8fd5-56c96b9a7274.notes: So my book is called Playful Pottery.

3bda6137-51d2-46b2-9309-113a1e5a6273.notes: I wanted something that was a more simplified book about pottery for beginners.

e553009a-d9df-4275-9663-cef70f4404a5.notes: But also, I really want people to be creative and be kind to themselves.

363e0c4a-e1f9-4a1c-b4fc-fd9dbe2e34d7.notes: I think that there's a pressure to produce things. As a creative person, but not to be kind of kind to yourself about what the process is going to be like,

e44b5c98-6dc5-4736-84ff-ee136d752915.notes: When you're kind to yourself, you are rolling with the punches. You are more open to be flexible with your designs, and you can end up with something that turns out way better than your original design.

700ced05-97e0-4313-bd1f-a2f74fca8fce.notes: I think that it's so easy to desire so many things, um, that we actually don't need.

7e3ba61a-8162-4c67-9b85-d18f5c19daa5.notes: Um, but also just the value of keeping something for a very long time.

85b2ca04-ee8a-4538-bc5a-92c2e7cd1ca8.notes: with lockdown, people really sat in their houses and realized that the things that were surrounding them weren't bringing them joy. And I think that's why ceramics has had such a big surge.

8509fe24-3951-419a-aa00-21c07255b510.notes: Hi, I'm Viviana matsuda. Um, I do pottery for a living. My brand name is Mud Witch. Um, yeah. I'm a full time potter.

881aed5c-7eef-4e15-84c9-cae867134e3a.notes: So my book is called Playful Pottery.

fa9a1ebb-21b1-47c4-b4a1-7142008d843c.notes: I wanted something that was a more simplified book about pottery for beginners.

4493acce-cc86-41e1-8fa8-78bfe8ad9504.notes: I feel like what I always saw or referenced were these, like, big, hearty old school books that never really talked about color had super fun things to do in them. Um, very like old school pottery.

59dc59f7-39a7-4f7e-92f2-c2c1cf43260b.notes: I hope the book provides to its readers at, um, like a good reference for just general, um, clay knowledge.

847c074f-ad7f-4df9-a45c-9385586a9419.notes: But also, I really want people to be creative and be kind to themselves.

68e164e8-293d-427a-b543-f7d66b79edca.notes: I think that there's a pressure to produce things. As a creative person, but not to be kind of kind to yourself about what the process is going to be like,

a91256f5-b86e-4366-b3ab-24fda5fc8fb1.notes: I think being open minded when it comes to design is really important.

25c0b86e-d95d-4491-93a2-0ecc4e56e925.notes: And then you're like, well, what if this looked slightly different? Or what if this, instead of a tulip was a daffodil? And let's try to achieve that. So it's kind of like sitting at the wheel and just like letting yourself adjust, grow whatever ideas and just see if they're achievable.

295dc021-0128-410c-9897-24eead6d1d5c.notes: Um, so my voice and style for mud, which it's kind of a funny thing where when I was learning to do ceramics, I was also learning about the body positivity movement.

1cc4ef52-8e4c-4178-942c-0678f25aa8fa.notes: And I was like starting to make these like chubby shapes and they're literally called this is the Chubby Mug. This is the Venus mug

e4881014-cc83-4c0c-8752-2d6f28f9bcc5.notes: I think those two things kind of just mushed together the learning clay and the body positivity.

f417ada1-9462-4854-a862-68fe326b29bc.notes: they were originally supposed to be kind of like an abstract like vision of, of people, like different bodies sitting, dancing, whatever.

f4835fa1-4d85-4f6e-8da8-b0b4867a3476.notes: they used to only use raw clay, which is all skin tones, which is really interesting.

d3522de7-521b-476e-bdee-a6ac208074b6.notes: so I used like 11 different types of clay, and they were all the range of skin tones. Um, so they were like naked.

57193451-4cab-4980-bd49-0572f451463b.notes: and then I was like, well, let's slap some color on these, um, let's clothe these babes.

32eae24a-a126-4198-b44e-76f7c9a8c4fe.notes: the style has grown into something that now is just like, fun.

fa423965-1414-4394-bcb9-30ed756e4ad1.notes: I, It started off as one thing, and now it's just like, I just want to make something that, like, makes people smile.
